pr_title: sessionctx: support signing and checking tokens
pr_body:

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #36029

Problem Summary:
To enable token-based authentication, the server should first be able to load a cert, create a token, sign the token, and check the token.

The process of token-based authentication:
1. Before migrating the session, the proxy requires a token from server A.
2. Server A generates a token and signs it with a private key defined in the certificate.
3. The proxy authenticates with server B and sends the signed token as the password.
4. Server B checks the signature with the public key defined in the certificate and then verifies the token.

The authentication process will be implemented in another PR, this PR only handles certificates and tokens.

The certificates should be rotated periodically by administrators or the TiDB operator, so a loader keeps loading the certificate periodically.

The certificates on all the servers should be the same all the time. Just in case of using different certificates to sign and check, a server should keep the old certificate for a while. A server will try both the 2 certificates to check the signature.

### What is changed and how it works?

- A cert creator is used to create certs for testing.
- A loader to load the cert periodically. It will be called in a future PR.
- Sign and check the token with RSA, ECDSA, and ED25519 signature algorithms.
- Setting the cert and key path, which will be called by system variables in a future PR.

issue_context.title: support signing and checking tokens
issue_context.body:
This is a preparing issue for https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/35913.
In token-based authentication, the server must be able to load a cert, sign a token, and check the token.

review_comments: In the future we need to add this error to the metrics(grafana), but not in this PR.

So if the first cert is expired, the loop is over? We don't loop over all certs because of descending `expireTime`? That should be avoided(if there are not too many certs) or at least documented somewhere. Same for L232.
The `expireTime` of certs must be descending because of the order of adding them into `certs`. Why should be avoided?
Since `ExpireTime = SignTime + tokenLifeTime`, what is the difference between this and `now.After(token.ExpireTime)`(line 110)?

I check both the SignTime and ExpireTime for better safety.
One may forge a very long lifetime to brute force attack:
- The SignTime is now, say, 2022-7-1.
- The token lifetime is set to 1 year, so the ExpireTime is 2023-7-1.
- After one year later, at 2023-6-30, he finally gets the right signature.

More specifically, I should check:
- `now.Before(token.ExpireTime)`
-  `now.After(token.SignTime)`
-  `token.SignTime.Add(tokenLifetime).Equal(token.ExpireTime)`

However, there may be 2 problems:
- The `tokenLifetime` may change between TiDB versions.
- There may exist time bias between TiDB instances.

I want to have a tolerance for these situations.
